cells.quote: As shown in Figure 3, the states in our sample exhibit remarkably high levels of policy adherence, with reclassification rates among eligible students ranging from 96 to 98 percent. This indicates that nearly all students who demonstrate ELP, per state-specific guidelines, are designated as former ELs. That said, it is not universally applied across policy structures. Of all states in the sample, State D (the only state that mandates proficiency in end-of-grade assessments for reclassification) exhibits a relatively lower degree of policy adherence, such that close to 4.5 percent of students who meet test-based eligibility criteria are not reclassified.
cells.note: Descriptive Figure 3 comparison based on student-level administrative records from multiple districts across four states; states and policies were not randomly assigned.

D.treatment: complex policies including ELP and non-ELP criteria

cells.quote: Next, we consider how the percentage of students eligible for reclassification changes after accounting for non-ELP requirements in addition to ELP criteria. By design, States A and B do not observe differences since their reclassification policies do not include non-ELP requirements. In contrast, States C and D experience notable changes, with the percentage of students meeting both ELP and non-ELP criteria dropping significantly. In State D, for instance, the eligibility rate decreases from nearly 40 percent to just over 7 percent.
cells.note: The study reports descriptive comparisons across states; policy complexity was not experimentally assigned.

cells.quote: Since the 70’s (and I was there to see it), there has indeed been a dramatic change in the field. It would be hard for young researchers today to appreciate the dominance of behavioral and cognitive behavioral perspectives in that time and the separation of that work from the largely non-empirically based but passionate humanistic perspectives of the era. Yes, the 70’s was a time when the undercurrents of change in empirical traditions began, but over the next years, the field of motivation in education specifically evolved from an emphasis on the external control of behaviors via contingent rewards, toward an emphasis on the inherent propensities and psychological needs of the active learner.

cells.quote: One key finding of this review is that it only identified 22 RCTs, which is a small number of gold-standard intervention studies given the huge number of interventions that claim to help poor readers.
